sections.title: What this is
sections.lede: Game-style Rubik's cube tutorial PWA — beginner to CFOP, with camera scan to solve your own cube.

items: Teaches anyone to solve a Rubik's cube, from zero.
Beginner method first, then CFOP for speed.
Scan your own cube with the camera and get guided to solve it.
Installs on your phone, works offline, no sign-in.
Public, free, hosted on GitHub Pages.
9 beginner levels: notation, the 7 stages, then a full solve. Levels list: Design tab → 02 — Levels.
XP, ranks and 13 badges; levels unlock in order. Rules: Design tab → 03 — Game.
Solve my cube: scan it with the camera (or tap colors in), check it, then get guided move by move.
8 CFOP levels after the beginner ones: cross, F2L, 4-look last layer, full PLL, full solve. Plus a Timer for real-cube solves.

decisions.question: Is the architecture and milestone order OK?
decisions.notes: milestone order M1–M7 and the app parts in `01-architecture.md` both agreed 2026-11-04.

decisions.question: Should colorblind players get symbols on stickers?
decisions.trigger: before the 3D cube (M1) and check-and-fix screen (M4).
decisions.notes: cube colors red/orange and green/blue are hard for colorblind players. **Decision:** stickers always keep their colors. An "ADA support" setting, off by default, adds a shape on each color (one shape per color).

decisions.question: How many levels, and what does each teach?
decisions.trigger: before M2. **Decision:** 9 beginner levels (0–8), listed in `02-levels.md`. Decided by Claude under the standing go-ahead; Rob to review.

decisions.question: What are the XP amounts, badges, and unlock rules?
decisions.trigger: before M3. **Decision:** in `03-game.md`. Decided by Claude under the standing go-ahead; Rob to review.

decisions.question: How does the camera read colors?
decisions.trigger: before M5. **Decision:** in `04-camera-scan.md`. Decided by Claude under the standing go-ahead; Rob to review.
decisions.notes: red vs. orange is the hard case under indoor light.

decisions.question: Should the solve path give the shortest solution, or the beginner-method one?
decisions.notes: beginner-method moves match what the player learned; shortest is ~20 moves but hard to follow. **Decision:** guide with the method the player has learned (beginner or CFOP), step by step, each step explained. No shortest-solution option.

decisions.question: Keep or remove the Docker stub?
decisions.notes: the app is static files on GitHub Pages; Docker isn't needed to run it. **Decision:** keep it for local testing. The image builds the app and serves it with nginx on port 4027 (`make serve-image`).

decisions.question: Track usage on the public site?
decisions.notes: no tracking keeps the "no personal data" promise simple. **Decision:** no tracking of any kind.

decisions.question: Teach full OLL (57 cases)?
decisions.trigger: players finishing Full PLL and asking for more.
decisions.notes: v1 teaches 2-look OLL (9 sequences). Full OLL is 57 sequences, an advanced step most cubers learn after full PLL. Decided by Claude under the standing go-ahead; Rob to review.

decisions.question: Which license for the public repo?
decisions.notes: the repo is public, but without a license others have no right to reuse the code. Rob's call.

docs.title: Cube Solver — Mission Statement
docs.html:
Cube Solver — Mission Statement

Mission

  • Teach anyone to solve a Rubik's cube, starting from zero.
  • Make learning feel like a game: levels, XP, badges.
  • Take players from the beginner method all the way to CFOP.
  • Solve the player's own scrambled cube, step by step, from a camera scan.

Who this is for

  • The public: anyone with a 3x3 cube and a phone or computer.
  • Includes total beginners who have never solved a cube.
  • Includes beginners who want to move up to speedcubing (CFOP).
  • Mostly on phones, cube in one hand, so big buttons and few words.

What the tool must do

  1. Teach the beginner layer-by-layer method, one stage per level.
  2. Teach CFOP after the beginner method, as later levels.
  3. Show every move on a 3D cube the player can turn and replay.
  4. Award XP and badges, and lock later levels until earlier ones are passed.
  5. Scan the player's real cube with the camera, one face at a time.
  6. Let the player check and fix scanned colors before solving.
  7. Guide the player through solving their scanned cube, move by move.
  8. Save progress on the device.
  9. Install to the home screen and work offline.

Hard constraints

  • PWA: installs like an app, runs offline after the first visit.
  • No server: static files only, hosted on GitHub Pages.
  • No accounts: no sign-in, no personal data collected.
  • Camera stays on the device: images are never uploaded.
  • Works on phones and desktops: iPhone Safari, Android Chrome, desktop browsers.

Decisions already made

  • Vite + TypeScript, no framework.
  • Three.js for the 3D cube.
  • Hosted on GitHub Pages from mr-flowjangles/cubeSolver, public repo.
  • Progress saved on the device only.
  • Camera scan for entering a real cube, with a check-and-fix screen.

Scope explicitly out of v1

  • Accounts and syncing progress across devices.
  • Puzzles other than the 3x3 cube.

Working style

  • Design before code. Decisions are written in docs/ first.
  • Deferred decisions go in docs/99-open-questions.md.
  • A question found during coding pauses the work until the docs answer it.
  • Three-part version numbers, one PR per version.
  • Release notes live under Versions/.

What this brief deliberately does NOT prescribe

  • How many levels, and what each one teaches.
  • XP amounts, badge list, and unlock rules.
  • How the solver works out the moves for a scanned cube.
  • How the camera reads sticker colors.
  • Visual style and sound.

toc.text: What this brief deliberately does NOT prescribe

docs.title: 00 — Overview
docs.html:
00 — Overview

What this tool does

  • A free web game that teaches you to solve a Rubik's cube.
  • Levels walk you from your first solve to speedcubing (CFOP).
  • Earn XP and badges as you pass levels.
  • Scan your own scrambled cube with your phone camera.
  • The game then guides you through solving it, move by move.

Who it's for

  • Anyone with a 3x3 cube, mostly on a phone.
  • Total beginners through people learning to speedcube.

v1 scope

In scope:

  • Beginner layer-by-layer method, one level per stage.
  • CFOP levels after the beginner method.
  • 3D cube that shows every move, with replay.
  • XP, badges, and locked levels.
  • Camera scan, with a screen to check and fix colors.
  • Guided solve of the scanned cube.
  • Progress saved on the device.
  • Installs to the home screen, works offline.

Explicitly out of scope for v1:

  • Accounts and syncing across devices.
  • Puzzles other than the 3x3.

High-level flow

Learn path:   pick level ──▶ watch moves on 3D cube ──▶ practice ──▶ pass ──▶ XP + badge ──▶ next level unlocks

Solve path:   camera scan ──▶ check & fix colors ──▶ work out the moves ──▶ guide player move by move

Reading order

Design (the what and why):

  1. mission.md — why this exists.
  2. This doc — the what.
  3. 01-architecture.md — the parts of the app and how they connect.

Build (the how and when):

  1. 07-build-plan.md — milestones, ordered tasks, checkboxes.

Tracking:

  1. 99-open-questions.md — what's not decided yet.

North-star direction (post-v1)

  • Not decided. See 99-open-questions.md.

docs.title: 01 — Architecture
docs.html:
01 — Architecture

Status: agreed 2026-11-04.

The spine

  • Everything passes around one thing: the cube state.
  • Cube state = the color of all 54 stickers.
  • The camera produces a cube state.
  • The solver reads a cube state and returns a list of moves.
  • The 3D cube draws a cube state and animates moves on it.
  • Lessons start from a set cube state and check the player's result.
camera scan ──▶ cube state ──▶ solver ──▶ moves ──▶ 3D cube (shows each move)
lesson      ──▶ cube state ──────────────────────▶ 3D cube ──▶ pass/fail ──▶ XP

Why this shape

  • Each part can be built and tested alone.
  • The camera can be swapped for tap-to-fix input without touching the solver.
  • Solver logic is tested with plain data, no 3D or camera needed.
  • No server: everything runs in the browser.

Modules

Cube model

  • Holds a cube state and applies moves (R, U, F, L, D, B and their variants).
  • Standard cube notation, the same one every tutorial uses.
  • No drawing, no camera. Pure data, heavily tested.

3D cube

  • Draws a cube state with Three.js.
  • Animates moves, lets the player spin the view, replays steps.

Solver

  • Beginner solver: works out moves stage by stage, same stages the lessons teach.
  • CFOP: uses the standard published move-sequence lists (F2L, OLL, PLL).
  • Output: moves grouped by stage, so the guide can explain each one.

Lessons

  • One level per stage: what it teaches, start position, pass check.
  • Lesson content is data, not code.

Game

  • XP, badges, unlock rules.
  • Saves progress on the device.

Camera scan

  • Reads one face at a time from the camera.
  • Turns sticker colors into a cube state.
  • Ends on the check-and-fix screen.

App shell

  • Screens and navigation.
  • PWA setup: offline, installable.

The contract: cube state

// 54 stickers, 9 per face, faces in the order U, R, F, D, L, B.
// Each sticker is the face it belongs to when solved.
type Face = "U" | "R" | "F" | "D" | "L" | "B";
type CubeState = Face[]; // length 54
type Move = string; // standard notation: "R", "U'", "F2", ...
  • Same layout most cube solvers use, so published test cases work as-is.

File layout

cubeSolver/
├── docs/
├── site/               # Mission Control
├── src/
│   ├── cube/           # cube model
│   ├── render/         # 3D cube
│   ├── solver/
│   ├── lessons/
│   ├── game/
│   ├── scan/           # camera scan
│   └── app/            # screens, PWA setup
└── tests/

Who talks to whom

PartOwnsTalks to
Cube modelcube state, moveseveryone
3D cubedrawing, animationcube model
Solverworking out movescube model
Lessonslevel content, pass checkscube model, solver
GameXP, badges, unlocks, saveslessons
Camera scanreading colorscube model
App shellscreens, offline, installall of the above

Non-goals

  • No server, no database, no accounts.
  • No puzzles other than the 3x3.

docs.title: 02 — Levels
docs.html:
02 — Levels

Status: decided by Claude under Rob's standing go-ahead, 2026-11-04. Rob to review.

Every level is a tutorial (Rob, 2026-11-04)

This is a tutorial, not a test. Shipped levels drop the player on a scrambled cube and say "figure it out". That is wrong and is being rebuilt (M8).

Every level runs in three parts:

  1. Show it. The app does the step slowly on the cube. Plain words say what is happening and why.
  2. Walk through it. The player does it while the app names each move, lights up the piece being moved and its target spot, and makes the right button glow. A wrong turn is undone with a correction.
  3. Then try it. Only now a practice cube, with Hint and Show me. The first cubes are easy (one piece left), then harder.

Rules that follow from it:

  • Never ask the player to do something the level hasn't shown.
  • Every move on screen gets a plain-words reason ("this lifts the white edge out of the way").
  • Pieces are named by their colors ("the white–orange edge") and lit up, not described by position alone.
  • White cross uses the daisy: put the 4 white edges around the yellow center on top (visible), then match each with its center and turn it down with F2.

How the three parts are built (v0.8.4):

  • Show it and Walk through it use the same demo cube every time.
  • The moves come from the solver, so they are the moves Hint and Show me use.
  • A half turn the buttons don't have (U2) is two taps.
  • The daisy never turns the left, back or bottom: the player can't see them. It turns the whole cube instead.
  • The daisy never knocks a white edge off the top on the way.
  • White edges already finished on the bottom stay there.
  • Try it has 3 practice cubes: one step left, about three steps left, then fully mixed. The level passes on the third.
  • Levels after White cross already run in three parts. A move with no reason of its own says what it does in words, e.g. "The right side goes up."[1]

Beginner method (M2)

  • The standard 7-stage layer-by-layer method, white on the bottom.
  • White on the bottom from the start, the same as CFOP, so moving up later needs no re-learning.
  • One level per stage, plus a notation level first and a full solve last.
#LevelPassed whenSequence taught
0Learn the controls11 swipes, then the trick: the same 4 moves six timesR U R' U' (6 times brings the cube back)
1White cross4 white edges on the bottom, matching centersnone — the daisy, then F2 for each edge
2White cornerswhite layer doneR U R' U' (repeat)
3Middle edgesfirst two layers doneU R U' R' U' F' U F / U' L' U L U F U' F'
4Yellow crossyellow plus on topF R U R' U' F'
5Yellow edgestop edges match centersR U R' U R U2 R' U
6Yellow corners into placetop corners in the right spotsU R U' L' U R' U' L
7Twist yellow cornerscube solvedR' D' R D (repeat)
8Full solvecube solved from a full scrambleall of the above

Level 0: learn to turn the cube[1]

  • Written for a 10-year-old. No letters: the arrow shows every move.
  • One line at the top: "Learn to turn the cube. Swipe where the arrow shows." No goal paragraph, no list.
  • Part 1: 11 swipes, one plain sentence each, e.g. "Swipe the right side up." The whole cube turns both ways: left, then back to the right.[1]
  • Every move prints a line in a list under the cube, e.g. "The right side went up."
  • Part 2, the trick: a fresh solved cube. Follow the arrows for the same 4 moves, 6 times (24 swipes). The cube gets mixed up, then comes back solved.
  • The trick is R U R' U' six times, which always returns the cube to where it started (checked by the app's own cube model in the tests). The letters show only as a small caption.
  • Passing the level means finishing the trick.

Level words checked by a kid test[1]

  • Each level's words were written as code and run on 200 practice cubes, as a 10-year-old who knows only what the screen says. A test repeats it on 20 cubes per level.
  • Every step the words left out is now said: how to lift an edge into the daisy, turning the whole cube so the spot is at front-right, which center means Edge right, how to pop out a stuck edge, and the last top turn.
  • Full solve lists every sequence, so it can be done without Hint.
  • Second round.[1] The words never say "hold". They say "turn the whole cube" or "turn the top", because the two give different results.
  • Front-right and the L's back-left are said in plain words where they're first used.
  • Full solve opens with a one-line recap of every level.
  • Every move in Show it and Walk through it gives a reason, e.g. "Corner sequence, round 2 of 3, move 3 of 4: the right side goes down."
  • Levels 2 and 3 light the piece being placed and its home. Levels 4–7 move many pieces at once, so nothing lights, and Show it doesn't promise it.
  • Each beginner demo cube is the shortest of 40 that plays every sequence the level teaches.

CFOP (M6)

  • Unlocks after Full solve.
  • Teaches the "4-look last layer" first: the standard first step into CFOP.
  • Then Full PLL (all 21 cases) and a full CFOP solve.
#LevelPassed whenSequences taught
9Cross in one gowhite cross done; Hint shows the shortestnone
10F2L pairsfirst two layers done6 short inserts
11OLL 1: yellow crossyellow plus on topLine, L shape
12OLL 2: yellow facewhole top yellowSune, Antisune, H, Pi, Headlights, T, Bowtie
13PLL 1: cornerstop corners in placeT-perm, Y-perm
14PLL 2: edgescube solvedUa, Ub, H, Z
15Full PLLa random PLL case solvedall 21 PLLs
16CFOP solvecube solved from a full scrambleall of the above
  • CFOP levels get extra buttons: M, M2, r, f, x.
  • Full OLL (57 cases) is not in v1 — see open questions.
  • Solve my cube guides with CFOP once F2L pairs is passed.

Timer

  • For real-cube solves: scramble shown, tap (or Space) to start and stop.
  • Shows best time and average of 5 (last 5, drop best and worst).
  • Under 60 s and under 30 s earn badges; no XP, since times can't be checked.

Controls

  • No buttons. You turn the cube by swiping on it.[1]
  • Swipe a sticker: the row or column under your finger turns the way you swiped.[2]
  • Swipe beside the cube: turns the whole cube. Left or right is y, up or down is x. Swipe left twice and the back becomes the front.[1]
  • Arrows only, no letters.[1] The arrow on the cube shows every move: in lessons, in Hint, and in the guided solve of your own cube. Whole-cube turns show the arrow beside the cube.
  • Letters stay only as a small caption under each sequence on a level page and in the guided solve, for anyone who wants them for a real cube.[1]
  • Tap a sequence and the arrow walks you through it on the cube, one move at a time, so a player never has to read the letters.[1] It works in Try it and on the PLL and full-solve levels, and doesn't count as help.
  • Hint says the step in words and puts the arrow on the cube for each move of it.[1]
  • No dimming. The cube keeps its real colors while an arrow shows; lessons still light the piece being moved and where it goes.[1]
  • The FRONT / TOP / RIGHT tags hide while an arrow shows, so nothing covers it.
  • Arrows go on the front first, then the right side, then the top or bottom. Back turns show on the right side's back column.
  • Turning the whole cube in a lesson is fine.[1] Walk through it renames the moves left for the new front. Hint and Show me plan from the cube as it is.
  • Half turns (U2) are two swipes.
  • Two-layer turns are two swipes: r is R then M', f is F then S.
  • Beginner levels have no middle rows, since turning one moves the centers. Swiping one says so. CFOP levels and free play allow middle rows.
  • Keyboard: a letter turns clockwise, Shift+letter the other way: U R F D L B, y, x, and M in CFOP.
  • FRONT, TOP and RIGHT tags float next to the cube and never turn: they name places, not colors.
  • A swipe that starts while the cube is turning is ignored, because the stickers aren't in place yet.
  • Caption letters follow standard notation, from a research pass of ruwix, J Perm, the official Rubik's guide and the cubing.js viewer.

How a level works

  • Practice cube: a random scramble with every earlier stage already done.
  • Level 7 (twist yellow corners): easier practice cubes have fewer twisted corners, never a cube stopped part-way, because part-way the bottom is scrambled.
  • Hint shows the next step in words and moves.
  • Show me plays the next step on the cube.
  • New cube gives a fresh practice cube.
  • Levels 1–2 show the cube from below, so the white side is visible.

How the guide works out the moves

  • Cross: finds the fewest turns for each edge, one edge at a time.
  • Every later stage: tries short combinations of top turns, whole-cube turns and that stage's taught sequence.
  • So Hint and Show me only ever use what the level teaches.
  • Beginner: tested on 500 random scrambles; slowest about a quarter second.
  • CFOP: tested on 500 random scrambles; slowest about half a second. Times depend on the device.
  • Every CFOP sequence is checked by the cube model: last-layer ones keep the bottom two layers, and the 21 PLLs are all different cases.

Footnotes

  • [1] Design decision, 2026-11-09.
  • [2] Design decision, 2026-11-06.

03 — Game

Status: decided by Claude under Rob's standing go-ahead, 2026-11-04. Rob to review.

XP

EventXP
Pass a level, first time100
Pass Full solve, first time300

First pass of a level without Hint or Show me+50 bonus
  • The no-help bonus doesn't apply to Learn the controls (it has no Hint).

Ranks

RankXP
Newcomer0
Turner200
Layer Builder500
Solver1000
Cube Master2000
Speedcuber4000

Badges

  • One badge each for passing: Learn the controls, White cross, White corners, Middle edges, Yellow cross, Twist yellow corners, Full solve.
  • On My Own: pass any level without Hint or Show me.
  • Solo Solver: pass Full solve without Hint or Show me.
  • Five Solves: pass Full solve 5 times.
  • 3-Day Streak / 7-Day Streak: pass a level on that many days in a row.
  • Beginner Graduate: pass every beginner level.

Unlocks

  • Learn the controls is always open.
  • Each level unlocks when the one before it is passed.
  • Free play is always open.

Saving

  • Saved in the browser on this device only. No account, nothing sent anywhere.
  • Clearing the browser's site data resets progress.
  • Private browsing: progress lasts only for that visit.

docs.title: 04 — Camera scan
docs.html:
04 — Camera scan

Status: decided by Claude under Rob's standing go-ahead, 2026-11-04. Rob to review.

Flow

  • Solve my cube → Scan with camera.
  • Scan 6 faces in order: top, front, right, back, left, bottom.
  • Each face goes inside a 3×3 guide; the middle cell is ringed in the color it should be.
  • After 6 faces, the flat cube map opens with a "compare and fix" note.
  • Check & solve then works the same as tapping colors in.

How colors are read

  • Each sticker is read from the middle of its cell, using the median to ignore glare.
  • The six center stickers show what each color looks like under the player's own light.
  • Every other sticker gets the closest center color (CIE Lab color space, lightness counted half).
  • Each color is then re-averaged from all its stickers, and stickers re-assigned.
  • At most 9 stickers get each color.
  • If a piece comes out impossible, the least-certain stickers are swapped until every piece is real.

Privacy

  • Camera frames are read in the page and never uploaded or saved.

Tested here

  • Color reading: 50 random cubes each under daylight, warm bulb, cool LED and dim-room light; at most 1 wrong sticker per light.
  • Camera flow: a fake camera feed in headless Chrome; sampled colors matched the feed within 1 unit.

Not tested here

  • Real phone cameras (iPhone, Android) with a real cube.

docs.title: 05 — Phone check
docs.html:
05 — Phone check

What can only be checked on a real phone. Do it once on an iPhone and once on an Android.

Open https://mr-flowjangles.github.io/cubeSolver/ in Safari (iPhone) or Chrome (Android).

Install and offline

  • Add to Home Screen (iPhone: Share → Add to Home Screen; Android: menu → Install app).
  • Open it from the home screen icon. It opens full screen, no browser bar.
  • Turn on airplane mode, close and reopen it. It still works.

Cube and levels

  • Drag the cube to spin it. Tap move buttons; turns animate smoothly.
  • Pass Learn the controls. XP and a badge appear.
  • Close the app and reopen. Progress is still there.
  • Turn on ADA support. Shapes appear on stickers.

Camera scan (needs a real cube)

  • Solve my cube → Scan with camera. The camera asks for permission, then shows the guide.
  • Scan all 6 faces in normal room light.
  • Count wrong stickers on the check screen: ____ (expect 0–2).
  • Fix any, tap Check & solve, follow the guide to a solved cube.

Timer

  • Time one real solve. Best and average show.

Report anything that fails; it becomes a fix before v1.0.0.

docs.title: 07 — Build plan
docs.html:
07 — Build plan

The implementation order is the order in this doc. Milestones are sequential, tasks within a milestone are ordered. We check the boxes as we go. When a milestone is fully checked, the next one starts.

If something forces us off this plan (a discovered constraint, a customer arriving early, etc.), we update this doc first, then change course. Don't drift silently.

The convention is ## M<N> — {Title} so make version-M<N> can auto-resolve the milestone title from this file.

The Now: line below names the milestone(s) being worked on, comma-separated when there is more than one. Mission Control's phase pill and banner read it (make catalog).

Status: milestone order M1–M7 agreed 2026-11-04.

Now: M8

v1 — Definition of Done

v1 ships when all of the following are true:

  • Live on GitHub Pages, installable on iPhone and Android.
  • Works offline after the first visit.
  • A beginner can go from level 1 to a full solve using only the app.
  • CFOP levels are playable.
  • Camera scan of a real cube leads to a guided solve.
  • Every level walks the player through: show it, walk through it, then try it.
  • All milestones below are checked.
  • README.md has a quickstart.

M0 — Foundations

Goal: project skeleton and dev environment ready, no feature code yet.

  • Initialize git repo, add .gitignore and README.md, make initial commit of design docs.
  • Replace placeholders across the repo.
  • Add package.json (Vite, TypeScript, Three.js, Vitest, Prettier).
  • Wire up make setup / make test / make lint / make format.
  • Verify make ci passes on an empty test suite.
  • Docker image for local testing: make image, make smoke passes.
  • Verify versioning ceremony: ./scripts/new-version.sh --dry-run "Smoke Test".
  • Fill in docs/mission.md and docs/00-overview.md.
  • Sketch docs/01-architecture.md.
  • Fill in Versions/v0/v0.0/release-notes.md for the bootstrap commit.

Done when: project builds, tests run, versioning ceremony runs cleanly, mission/overview/architecture have v1 content.

M1 — Cube and live site

Goal: a 3D cube you can turn, live on GitHub Pages as an installable PWA.

  • Cube model: cube state, all moves, scramble. Fully tested.
  • 3D cube: draw, animate moves, spin the view.
  • PWA setup: offline, home-screen install.
  • GitHub Pages deploy on every push to main.

Done when: the live site shows a cube you can turn and scramble, on a phone, offline.

M2 — Beginner levels

Goal: the beginner method, taught one stage per level.

  • Beginner solver, stage by stage, tested on many random scrambles.
  • Level content for each beginner stage.
  • Lesson screen: explain, show moves, practice, pass check.

Done when: a player can learn a full beginner solve in the app.

M3 — Game layer

Goal: XP, badges, locked levels, saved progress.

  • XP and badge rules.
  • Unlocks: later levels locked until earlier ones are passed.
  • Progress saved on the device.

Done when: progress, XP, and badges survive closing and reopening the app.

M4 — Solve my cube

Goal: enter a real cube and get guided through solving it.

  • Tap-to-fix cube map (also used after camera scan).
  • Check that an entered cube is possible to solve.
  • Guided solve: one move at a time, grouped by stage.

Done when: a cube entered by hand is solved by following the guide.

M5 — Camera scan

Goal: scan a real cube instead of entering it by hand.

  • Camera capture, one face at a time, with a framing guide.
  • Read sticker colors.
  • Hand off to the check-and-fix screen.

Done when: a real cube scanned on iPhone and Android leads to a correct guided solve.

M6 — CFOP levels

Goal: teach CFOP after the beginner method.

  • Cross, F2L, OLL, PLL levels.
  • CFOP move-sequence lists, each checked by the cube model.
  • Solve timer and personal bests.

Done when: a player who finished the beginner levels can learn and practice full CFOP.

M7 — Launch

Goal: polished and public.

  • Test on real iPhone and Android devices. (blocked: needs Rob with real phones — see 05-phone-check.md)
  • README quickstart.
  • v1 Definition of Done all checked.

Done when: v1 Definition of Done is fully checked.

M8 — Guided lessons

Goal: every level teaches step by step (see 02-levels.md → Every level is a tutorial). Must land before M7's launch.

  • Lesson engine: Show it → Walk through it → Then try it, as data per level.
  • Walk-through: name each move, light the piece and its target, point an arrow at the swipe, undo wrong turns with a correction.
  • Plain-words reason for every move shown.
  • White cross rebuilt with the daisy (two parts: daisy, then cross).
  • Every beginner level rebuilt in the three parts.
  • Every CFOP level rebuilt in the three parts.
  • Practice cubes start easy (one piece left), then get harder.
  • Tests: each level's walk-through ends with the stage done.
  • Swipe-only controls: no buttons; arrow and letter show the next move; whole-cube turns allowed in lessons (see 02-levels.md → Controls).

Done when: a first-time player can finish every level without guessing, and a headless walk-through passes every level.

docs.title: 99 — Open questions
docs.html:
99 — Open questions

Decisions not made yet, with what would force them.

Is the architecture and milestone order OK?

Status: resolved 2026-11-04 Resolution trigger: before M1 starts. Notes: milestone order M1–M7 and the app parts in 01-architecture.md both agreed 2026-11-04.

Should colorblind players get symbols on stickers?

Status: resolved 2026-11-04 Resolution trigger: before the 3D cube (M1) and check-and-fix screen (M4). Notes: cube colors red/orange and green/blue are hard for colorblind players. Decision: stickers always keep their colors. An "ADA support" setting, off by default, adds a shape on each color (one shape per color).

How many levels, and what does each teach?

Status: resolved 2026-11-04 Resolution trigger: before M2. Decision: 9 beginner levels (0–8), listed in 02-levels.md. Decided by Claude under the standing go-ahead; Rob to review.

What are the XP amounts, badges, and unlock rules?

Status: resolved 2026-11-04 Resolution trigger: before M3. Decision: in 03-game.md. Decided by Claude under the standing go-ahead; Rob to review.

How does the camera read colors?

Status: resolved 2026-11-04 Resolution trigger: before M5. Decision: in 04-camera-scan.md. Decided by Claude under the standing go-ahead; Rob to review. Notes: red vs. orange is the hard case under indoor light.

Should the solve path give the shortest solution, or the beginner-method one?

Status: resolved 2026-11-04 Resolution trigger: before M4. Notes: beginner-method moves match what the player learned; shortest is ~20 moves but hard to follow. Decision: guide with the method the player has learned (beginner or CFOP), step by step, each step explained. No shortest-solution option.

Keep or remove the Docker stub?

Status: resolved 2026-11-04 Resolution trigger: M0 close-out. Notes: the app is static files on GitHub Pages; Docker isn't needed to run it. Decision: keep it for local testing. The image builds the app and serves it with nginx on port 4027 (make serve-image).

Track usage on the public site?

Status: resolved 2026-11-04 Resolution trigger: before M7. Notes: no tracking keeps the "no personal data" promise simple. Decision: no tracking of any kind.

Teach full OLL (57 cases)?

Status: deferred to v2 Resolution trigger: players finishing Full PLL and asking for more. Notes: v1 teaches 2-look OLL (9 sequences). Full OLL is 57 sequences, an advanced step most cubers learn after full PLL. Decided by Claude under the standing go-ahead; Rob to review.

Which license for the public repo?

Status: open Resolution trigger: before v1.0.0. Notes: the repo is public, but without a license others have no right to reuse the code. Rob's call.
